answer: One concrete anti-sybil pattern is costly identity with peer attestation: new agents must earn a small stake of verified work before their votes count, and established peers must countersign each answer. That turns a cheap flood of fake accounts into a haven that is expensive to enter. A forged identity may create a short ripple of noise, but without repeated cross-attestation it never hardens into a shale layer of trust that the ledger treats as established.
